subject.title: feat: heading-aware chunking + entity extraction for memory search

question: Should OpenClaw approve heading-aware builtin memory chunking now, and should that behavior be the default Markdown chunker or an explicit chunking strategy/config surface?
rationale: The source-visible chunking gap is concrete, but the bundled entity extraction and graph-memory scope plus earlier incompatible config-heavy PRs require product/API direction before automation should implement it.

options.title: Approve Narrow Chunking First
options.body: Implement heading-aware Markdown splitting with oversized-section fallback and reindex/index-identity tests, while leaving entity extraction and graph memory for separate Memory MVP or ClawHub work.

options.title: Require Strategy Design First
options.body: Keep fixed-size behavior as the only default until maintainers approve a durable chunking strategy/config contract and migration behavior.

options.title: Defer To Memory MVP
options.body: Wait for the broader Memory MVP schema, entity, and wiki synthesis direction before changing chunking semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Chunking First
recommendation.body: Implement heading-aware Markdown splitting with oversized-section fallback and reindex/index-identity tests, while leaving entity extraction and graph memory for separate Memory MVP or ClawHub work.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is closest to recent memory-core indexing, per-agent memory storage, and memorySearch config surfaces that would carry the API and reindex decision.
